drills.q: Front Door vs App Gateway - decision factors?
drills.a: Scope first: multi-region users/origins -> FD (anycast, edge TLS/cache, cross-region failover); single-region/internal -> AGW. Both do L7+WAF; adopt both only when global steering AND regional path-routing depth are both real requirements.

drills.q: Spoke A can't reach spoke B in hub-spoke. Explain and fix.
drills.a: Peering is non-transitive: hub must forward (NVA/gateway transit) with UDRs on spokes pointing inter-spoke CIDRs at hub plus symmetric return routes; verify Azure Firewall sees traffic only if UDRs force it.

drills.q: Random outbound resets appear after scale-out events. Diagnose.
drills.a: SNAT port exhaustion: per-instance port allocation shrinks as instance count grows (~1024 small instances) while connections multiply. Confirm via SNAT metrics; fix with NAT Gateway or sized LB outbound rules.

drills.q: On-prem clients bypass your private endpoint. Why?
drills.a: DNS split-brain: on-prem resolver lacks privatelink conditional forwarding so names resolve publicly. Add forwarders to Azure DNS or sync records; treat DNS records as IaC; test from failing vantage point.

drills.q: Lock App Gateway to Front Door-only traffic - three layers.
drills.a: NSG allow only AzureFrontDoor.Backend tag on AGW subnet; validate X-Azure-FDID header equals your FD ID via custom rule; optionally FD Premium Private Link origin eliminating AGW public IP entirely.

drills.q: Design ingress for 3-region app with WAF compliance and private backends.
drills.a: FD Premium WAF globally -> Private Link origins to zone-redundant AGW v2 per region locked via tag+FD-ID -> private-endpoint backends; probe-tuned origin groups, priority/weight failover, alias DNS record; rehearse regional kill switch.

drills.q: Post-Basic-LB-migration everything inbound is blocked. What changed?
drills.a: Standard SKU is secure-by-default: inbound flows need explicit NSG allow rules (Basic was open-by-default); also outbound stops until configured; public IPs must be Standard/static.

drills.q: Mystery 502s from Front Door with healthy-looking backends. First check?
drills.a: Health probe configuration: wrong path/port returning 404s marks all origins unhealthy -> 502s. Align probes with a real health endpoint; monitor probe-failure metrics before touching backends.

drills.q: When is ExpressRoute wasteful vs S2S VPN?
drills.a: Sub-Gbps sporadic/dev/test needs: VPN's near-zero idle cost and days-level provisioning beat circuit pricing and weeks-long lead times. ER earns keep at sustained multi-Gbps, compliance isolation, latency-sensitive replication.

Against: per-endpoint costs, DNS-as-critical-path complexity, hybrid forwarding sprawl. Counter: eliminates exfiltration classes, audit mandates private paths, DNS pain is one-time IaC investment. Verdict: PE-default for data services, selective elsewhere, DNS-as-code mandatory.
